messages.text: Humphries, Wade progress at World Grand Prix as Rock dumped out

metadata.summary: Luke Humphries was not punished for a raft of missed finishing doubles as he beat a below-par Dave Chisnall to reach the second round of the World Grand Prix in Leicester.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries and James Wade reach round two as Josh Rock and Chris Dobey dumped out | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries and James Wade reach round two as Josh Rock and Chris Dobey dumped out Luke Humphries - the new title favourite after Luke Littler's exit - beats below-par Dave Chisnall before appearing to shush member of crowd, will face Jermaine Wattimena next; other winners on Tuesday include Gian van Veen, Gary Anderson, Stephen Bunting and debutant Niels Zonneveld Wednesday 30 September 2026 00:02, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Humphries taunted a fan who seemingly agitated the former world champion following his World Grand Prix win over Dave Chisnall Luke Humphries was not punished for a raft of missed finishing doubles as he beat a below-par Dave Chisnall to reach the second round of the World Grand Prix in Leicester. Humphries - who has made the last three finals in this event, winning in 2023 ahead of two runners-up finishes since - is the new favourite to triumph this year following defending champion Luke Littler's shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night. Cool Hand, sporting a scab on his forehead he put down to an allergic reaction, defeated Chisnall 2-0 while averaging only 80.41 and going at 26 per cent on his doubles as he secured a second-round meeting with Chris Dobey's conqueror Jermaine Wattimena. metadata.summary: Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter.
metadata.content: Joss Buttler says Brendon McCullum's removal as England Test coach may have boosted Cricket World Cup chances | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Joss Buttler says Brendon McCullum's removal as England Test coach may have boosted Cricket World Cup chances Brendon McCullum left his role as England Test coach in July; Jos Buttler believes the move has allowed the New Zealander to focus solely on helping England win the Cricket World Cup; Buttler has been ruled out of the upcoming Pakistan white-ball tour due to injury Tuesday 29 September 2026 15:39, UK Image: Jos Buttler says Brendon McCullum (pictured) is 'all in' on helping England win the Cricket World Cup in 2027 Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter. McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties in July , with Stephen Fleming eventually named as his successor , but remained in charge of a limited-overs set-up that ended the summer with a record of 11 wins and two defeats. That included ODI series wins over India and Sri Lanka , raising England's stock in a format that has seen them decline since they became world champions in 2019. messages.text: Trent: I always believed I'd play for England again

metadata.summary: Trent Alexander-Arnold "always believed" he could play for England again following his period in the international wilderness under Thomas Tuchel.
metadata.content: Trent Alexander-Arnold 'always believed' he would play for England again after first start in over two years | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Trent Alexander-Arnold 'always believed' he would play for England again after first start in over two years Trent Alexander-Arnold grabbed an assist on his first start for England in over two years; England recovered from slow start to beat Czech Republic 2-0 in Prague to get Nations League campaign up and running, with second-half goals from Anthony Gordon and captain Harry Kane Tuesday 29 September 2026 23:33, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel praised Trent Alexander-Arnold's performance during England's 2-0 win over the Czech Republic. Trent Alexander-Arnold "always believed" he could play for England again following his period in the international wilderness under Thomas Tuchel. The 27-year-old defender made his first start for the Three Lions in almost two years in the 2-0 win over Czech Republic. Alexander-Arnold had fallen out of favour under Tuchel over the past year or so, missing out on the World Cup squad this summer. The Real Madrid player's last appearance for the national team came in June 2025, in a World Cup qualifier against Andorra. But the former Liverpool defender made a good impression on his return, grabbing an assist for Anthony Gordon's opening goal as England swatted aside 10-man Czech Republic.
